<a id="addressing"></a>

## Address plan

Every prefix an address sits in, and how full it is.

<a id="table-subnets"></a>

**Subnets**

| PREFIX | IP | VLANS | HOSTS | USED | FREE | UTIL | DEVICES |
|:---|---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10.10.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 2 | 252 | 0.8% | 2 |
| 10.20.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 2 | 252 | 0.8% | 2 |
| 10.30.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 2 | 252 | 0.8% | 2 |
| 10.252.0.0/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 2 | 0 | 100.0% | 2 |
| 10.253.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 2 | 252 | 0.8% | 2 |
| 10.254.0.0/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 2 | 0 | 100.0% | 2 |
| 10.255.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 3 | 251 | 1.2% | 3 |
| 198.51.100.0/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 2 | 0 | 100.0% | 2 |
| 198.51.100.4/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 2 | 0 | 100.0% | 2 |
| 198.51.100.8/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 2 | 0 | 100.0% | 2 |

HOSTS is the usable capacity of the prefix, USED the distinct addresses declared in it. Loopback and link-local prefixes are left out: they are scoped to one host or one link and say nothing about the plan.


<a id="vlans"></a>

## VLANs

Every VLAN, the prefixes carried in it and the elements that are in it.

<a id="table-vlan-summary"></a>

**VLANs**

| VLAN | NAME | ELEMENTS | PORTS |
|---:|:---|---:|---:|
| 100 | overlay | 2 | 2 |

Membership is derived: a host on an untagged access port counts as a member even though it declares no VLAN itself.

<a id="table-vlan-matrix"></a>

**VLAN, subnet and element matrix**

| VLAN | NAME | ELEMENT | PORTS | MODE | SUBNETS |
|---:|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 100 | overlay | [rtr-branch-b](devices/sites_branch-b_rtr-branch-b.md) | vxlan100 | access | — |
| 100 | overlay | [rtr-hq](devices/sites_hq_rtr-hq.md) | vxlan100 | access | — |

A row with no port is an element that reaches the VLAN over a link rather than by configuring it — a host behind an access port, or a hub.


<a id="tunnels"></a>

## Tunnels

Every overlay, with what it runs inside and what protects it.

<a id="table-tunnels"></a>

**Tunnels**

| NAME | STACK | VNI | ENCRYPTED | ENDS | ENDPOINTS |
|:---|:---|---:|:---|---:|:---|
| tunnels/wg-mesh | wireguard | - | yes | 3 | rtr-branch-a:wg0, rtr-branch-b:wg0, rtr-hq:wg0 |
| tunnels/ipsec-hq-b | ipsec | - | yes | 2 | rtr-branch-b:ipsec0, rtr-hq:ipsec0 |
| tunnels/vx-100 | vxlan over ipsec | 100 | underlay | 2 | rtr-branch-b:vxlan100, rtr-hq:vxlan100 |
| tunnels/gre-mgmt | gre over ipsec | - | underlay | 2 | rtr-branch-b:gre1, rtr-hq:gre1 |
| tunnels/ovpn-admin | openvpn | - | yes | 2 | pc-branch-b:tun0, rtr-hq:ovpn0 |

STACK reads outwards: 'vxlan over ipsec' is VXLAN carried inside the IPsec tunnel.

<a id="addressing"></a>

## Address plan

Every prefix an address sits in, and how full it is.

<a id="table-subnets"></a>

**Subnets**

| PREFIX | IP | VLANS | HOSTS | USED | FREE | UTIL | DEVICES |
|:---|---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10.10.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 2 | 252 | 0.8% | 2 |
| 10.20.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 2 | 252 | 0.8% | 2 |
| 10.30.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 2 | 252 | 0.8% | 2 |
| 10.252.0.0/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 2 | 0 | 100.0% | 2 |
| 10.253.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 2 | 252 | 0.8% | 2 |
| 10.254.0.0/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 2 | 0 | 100.0% | 2 |
| 10.255.0.0/24 | 4 | - | 254 | 3 | 251 | 1.2% | 3 |
| 198.51.100.0/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 1 | 1 | 50.0% | 1 |
| 198.51.100.4/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 1 | 1 | 50.0% | 1 |
| 198.51.100.8/30 | 4 | - | 2 | 1 | 1 | 50.0% | 1 |

HOSTS is the usable capacity of the prefix, USED the distinct addresses declared in it. Loopback and link-local prefixes are left out: they are scoped to one host or one link and say nothing about the plan.


<a id="vlans"></a>

## VLANs

Every VLAN, the prefixes carried in it and the elements that are in it.

<a id="table-vlan-summary"></a>

**VLANs**

| VLAN | NAME | ELEMENTS | PORTS |
|---:|:---|---:|---:|
| 100 | overlay | 2 | 2 |

Membership is derived: a host on an untagged access port counts as a member even though it declares no VLAN itself.

<a id="table-vlan-matrix"></a>

**VLAN, subnet and element matrix**

| VLAN | NAME | ELEMENT | PORTS | MODE | SUBNETS |
|---:|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 100 | overlay | [rtr-branch-b](../devices/sites_branch-b_rtr-branch-b.md) | vxlan100 | access | — |
| 100 | overlay | [rtr-hq](../devices/sites_hq_rtr-hq.md) | vxlan100 | access | — |

A row with no port is an element that reaches the VLAN over a link rather than by configuring it — a host behind an access port, or a hub.


<a id="cabling"></a>

## Cabling

What an installer would carry into the room.

<a id="table-cable-schedule"></a>

**Cable schedule**

| RUN | SEGMENT | CABLE | LABEL | MEDIUM | CATEGORY | SPEED | LENGTH | A END | A PORT | A POSITION | B END | B PORT | B POSITION |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|---:|---:|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| — | — | cbl-branch-a-pc | — | copper | cat6 | 1Gbps | — | [pc-branch-a](../devices/sites_branch-a_pc-branch-a.md) | enp3s0 | — | [rtr-branch-a](../devices/sites_branch-a_rtr-branch-a.md) | ether2 | — |
| — | — | cbl-branch-b-pc | — | copper | cat6 | 1Gbps | — | [pc-branch-b](../devices/sites_branch-b_pc-branch-b.md) | enp3s0 | — | [rtr-branch-b](../devices/sites_branch-b_rtr-branch-b.md) | ether2 | — |
| — | — | cbl-hq-srv | — | copper | cat6 | 1Gbps | — | [rtr-hq](../devices/sites_hq_rtr-hq.md) | eth1 | — | [srv-hq](../devices/sites_hq_srv-hq.md) | eno1 | — |

One row per cable document, which is one run somebody pulls: a link through a patch panel is several. RUN names the end-to-end link and SEGMENT which leg of it this is. 'netgraph export cable-list' writes the same rows as CSV, with the full location of both ends.


<a id="wireless"></a>

## Wireless

Every BSS: which radio beacons which SSID, on what channel, into which VLAN.

<a id="table-bss"></a>

**BSS and SSID plan**

_No radio is declared here._

One row per SSID per radio: a dual-band AP serving three networks has six.

|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| cable | cbl-wan-hq | [rtr-hq](../devices/sites_hq_rtr-hq.md) | eth0 | [wan-core](../devices/wan_wan-core.md) | ge-0/0/0 | [wan](wan.md) |
| cable | cbl-wan-branch-a | [rtr-branch-a](../devices/sites_branch-a_rtr-branch-a.md) | ether1 | [wan-core](../devices/wan_wan-core.md) | ge-0/0/1 | [wan](wan.md) |
| cable | cbl-wan-branch-b | [rtr-branch-b](../devices/sites_branch-b_rtr-branch-b.md) | ether1 | [wan-core](../devices/wan_wan-core.md) | ge-0/0/2 | [wan](wan.md) |

These links are deliberately absent from the diagrams and the cable schedule above, which cover this page's elements only. A far end with no page of its own is outside what this report documents at all.
